idh.reasoning: The lesion shows mild contrast enhancement (Enhancement Quality), a very low proportion of necrosis (Proportion Necrosis) and a low proportion of enhancing tumor (Proportion Enhancing). Cortical involvement is present (Cortical involvement) while deep white‑matter invasion (Deep WM invasion) and ependymal invasion (Ependymal (ventricular) Invasion) are absent, all features that favour an IDH‑mutant lower‑grade glioma. The only findings that argue against IDH‑mutant status are the multifocal presentation (Multifocal or Multicentric) and the very high oedema proportion (Proportion of Oedema), which are more typical of IDH‑wildtype glioblastoma. Balancing the evidence, the pre‑operative imaging most strongly supports IDH‑mutant status.

The necrosis proportion is very low (Proportion Necrosis) and the enhancement is not intense, arguing against grade 4, while the high oedema proportion (Proportion of Oedema) and multifocality (Multifocal or Multicentric) argue against a pure grade 2 lesion. overall_comment: The prediction relies on conventional MRI features only; lack of diffusion, perfusion and spectroscopy limits certainty, especially regarding the multifocal nature of the disease. Advanced imaging could better differentiate IDH‑wildtype glioblastoma from an IDH‑mutant astrocytoma and refine grade assessment.
